item.title: Jodeci Moves Ontario Anniversary Show From October To January
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Jodeci moved its Toyota Arena anniversary show from October 27 to January 16, with Eric Bellinger also on the bill.
item.content:encoded:
Jodeci fans will have to wait until next year for the group’s Ontario, California anniversary show. The concert had been set for October 27.

The Toyota Arena concert has moved to Saturday, January 16, 2027. The Ticketmaster event page confirms the switch from October 27, 2026, to the new January date.

Eric Bellinger is also on the bill. Toyota Arena lists an 8 P.M. show, with doors opening at 7 P.M. The venue remains the same, at 4000 East Ontario Center Parkway.

The stop is part of Jodeci’s “35th Anniversary Tour Of Forever My Lady.” The tour marks 35 years since the group’s 1991 debut album. Neither the venue’s event page nor Ticketmaster’s listing explains the date change.

For fans who already bought tickets, Ticketmaster’s rescheduling guidance says they remain valid for the new date. That includes purchased upgrades and add-ons such as parking. Fans who bought at a venue box office are directed to that box office for more details.

The Ontario listing also includes an all-sales-final notice stating there are no refunds or exchanges. Ticketmaster’s general policy leaves refund options to event organizers on a show-by-show basis. Ticket holders who cannot attend in January should check their order information for any options attached to their purchase.

The anniversary puts Forever My Lady back at the center of Jodeci’s live plans. The album introduced songs including “Forever My Lady,” “Stay,” and “Come & Talk To Me.” It later earned a triple-platinum certification from the RIAA.

The group has made other live plans around its catalog in recent years.

As AllHipHop previously reported, DeVanté Swing, Mr. Dalvin, K-Ci and JoJo announced a Las Vegas residency with runs set for March and July 2024. The venue was House of Blues inside Mandalay Bay.

The booking drew its name from their 1995 album The Show, the After Party, the Hotel.

The group’s official tour schedule now places Ontario within a January run through the West. San Francisco is set for January 8, followed by Inglewood on January 9 and El Cajon on January 10. Phoenix is listed for January 15. Toyota Arena comes next, ahead of a January 17 booking in Las Vegas.

item.title: TOB’s Lil Chris Says Chief Keef Didn’t Cause “Shake That” Streaming Removal
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: TOB's Lil Chris denied Chief Keef caused the "Shake That" takedown and alleged a false complaint pulled the viral go-go record.
item.content:encoded:
TOB’s Lil Chris said Chief Keef and his team were not behind the streaming removal of “Shake That (I Just Wanna Dance).”

Speaking with Aladdin Da Prince on 93.9 WKYS, Chris alleged that a false complaint caused the takedown. He also said Keef publicly supported the record.

The disruption followed a breakthrough for the go-go band. A Nucci’s Front Porch performance helped the song take off before Queen Peachifi’s dance carried it across TikTok.

Chris described TOB’s recent run as a “second half comeback” and said its audience extended to Poland, Tokyo and the United Kingdom. He said it was connecting young listeners with longtime go-go fans.

Getting go-go heard beyond Washington has long involved more than making a record people love. In a 2020 exclusive AllHipHop interview, DJ Kool pointed to the promotional support behind hits as one reason the genre had not enjoyed Hip-Hop’s wider commercial reach.

“We never got the proper marketing that Hip-Hop has got,” he said.

He used E.U.’s “Da Butt” as an example, crediting the machinery around the song and its connection to Spike Lee. The discussion accompanied TV One’s documentary “The Beat Don’t Stop,” which featured TOB alongside acts including Trouble Funk and Junk Yard Band.

DJ Kool also stressed recording during that earlier interview, saying “but it’s up to the group’s to get into the studio and make original material.”

A recent release offered another example of how go-go performances can move onto bigger distribution platforms.

Tone P’s “Tha Carry Out” recorded and executive produced Nino Paid’s live version of “Shine” with Hvmane Studios. Signal/Columbia Records acquired and released it, making it the platform’s first major-label release across streaming services.

The series turns familiar songs into go-go performances and has featured TOB among its guests.

That separate release put the live format into a label-backed rollout, while TOB’s current situation centers on getting its own viral record back to listeners.

At WKYS, Chris premiered an exclusive, newly recorded studio version of “Shake That (I Just Wanna Dance).” He announced plans to restore the song to streaming and said TOB had more original music planned for 2027.

item.title: 85 South Media Lands Tubi Distribution Deal
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: 85 South Media signed a Tubi distribution deal for a 10-episode collection featuring DC Young Fly, Karlous Miller and Chico Bean.
item.content:encoded:
Atlanta-based 85 South Media signed a Tubi distribution deal that will bring 10 episodes of “The 85 South Show” to the free streamer, according to Deadline.

The collection, “The Best Of The 85 South Show,” features DC Young Fly, Karlous Miller and Chico Bean. More programming is expected, though those projects have not been named.

Chad Oubre, the company’s CEO and co-founder, told Deadline the expansion would help 85 South reach more viewers as it continued to build its own business.

The comedians already had a movie in Tubi’s plans. On October 29, 2025, the company announced a four-film deal with Kevin Hart’s Hartbeat, including “85 South: Dead End.” The horror comedy follows the trio on a road trip through the South that leads them to a town people cannot leave.

That slate also included “Sundown,” a supernatural thriller written and directed by Kinigra Deon, who starred in it. Tubi placed both projects under its Tubi for Creators program, a push to bring creators’ work to the service and give them a wider audience.

DC Young Fly and Miller had another Tubi connection through T.I.’s “Da Partments”.

AllHipHop reported in 2023 that DC co-produced the Atlanta comedy while Miller and Lil Duval served as executive producers. All three appeared in the film, which T.I. wrote and directed.

The trio’s reach extended beyond their podcast. Netflix released their stand-up special “85 South: Ghetto Legends” in 2023.

It brought the same three comedians together for a stage show built around their podcast’s freewheeling comedy.

Their work also earned recognition at the 2024 NAACP Image Awards, where “The 85 South Show” won Outstanding Society and Culture Podcast. DC separately won the hosting award for “Celebrity Squares,” while “Wild ‘n Out,” which featured all three comics, won its reality program category.

Fans can also find the crew on Channel Eighty Five, their own subscription streaming service. Its catalog includes their classic shows and original series, with Desi Banks, Moneybag Mafia and Navv Greene among the featured comics. The service advertises its live-show library as an exclusive part of that offering and lists a monthly price of $8.50.

item.title: Learjet Crash Killed Nine As Jet Nosedives Into Florida Neighborhood
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.category: signs the world is coming to an end
item.description: Learjet disaster prompted a federal inquiry after a Caribbean itinerary became a deadly aviation emergency amid suburban streets.
item.content:encoded:
A Learjet traveling to the Bahamas ended in tragedy Sunday when the jet carrying nine people crashed near Florida homes and killed everyone aboard.

The Learjet 60 went down in a residential area near Cresthaven in Palm Beach County at approximately 12:50 p.m. Nov. 1, according to the Federal Aviation Administration. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy confirmed that all nine occupants died.

The aircraft had departed Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was traveling to North Eleuthera Airport in the Bahamas. Its flight ended near Military Trail, where emergency crews responded to flames and wreckage beside a residential community.

Video showed the jet descending steeply before exploding near a roadway. The impact left a burning crater and sent thick black smoke above the surrounding neighborhood. Homes and passing vehicles were close to where the aircraft struck, according to reporting by The Associated Press.

Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis said there were no immediate reports of people on the ground being injured or killed. Officials had not identified the nine occupants or released a breakdown of passengers and crew in the reporting reviewed for this story.

The emergency response disrupted traffic along Military Trail between Cresthaven Boulevard and 10th Avenue North. Palm Beach County sheriff’s deputies closed the roadway in both directions and asked motorists to avoid the area as authorities worked at the scene. Florida Power & Light crews also responded.

Federal investigators will now determine what caused the fatal descent. The FAA and National Transportation Safety Board are investigating, with the NTSB directing the inquiry and providing subsequent updates. The FAA cautioned that its initial information was preliminary and subject to change.

The NTSB said investigators would arrive Sunday and Monday, according to CNN. A Monday news conference was also planned. No cause had been established in the reports reviewed.

A flight intended to connect Texas with the Bahamas instead ended beside Florida homes. Nine people were killed, a neighborhood became an emergency scene and the explanation for the aircraft’s final descent remained unresolved.

item.title: The Weeknd Taps Faye Wong’s 1993 Classic For Asia-Exclusive “Hong Kong”
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: The Weeknd released "Hong Kong" across East and Southeast Asia, pairing Faye Wong's 1993 vocals with the city's film history.
item.content:encoded:
The Weeknd brought Hong Kong’s pop history into his latest release, using Faye Wong’s original Cantonese vocals on a song now streaming across East and Southeast Asia.

“Hong Kong” reached streaming services on October 31 after he introduced it at Kai Tak Stadium on October 24. That performance opened his four-night run in the city. The recording draws from Wong’s 1993 Cantopop song “Monsoon,” also known as “Seasonal Wind.”

The connection runs through film and music.

The cover uses a Hong Kong photograph from cinematographer Christopher Doyle’s own collection. Doyle shot Wong Kar-wai’s “Chungking Express,” which starred Wong and Tony Leung. The artwork links the release to the city’s screen history alongside the voice borrowed from its pop catalog.

That focus also shaped the visual shown during the live debut. Scenes of Victoria Harbour and a red-sailed junk, with the city’s red taxis and Mong Kok’s neon signs, share the screen, and the footage also took in dim sum spots and roasted chestnut sellers.

The locations stretched from the circular footbridge in Causeway Bay to the Tsim Sha Tsui waterfront and The Peninsula. Those details placed everyday food, street traffic and familiar gathering spots beside the harbor views, making the tribute specific to the city the crowd knew.

Viewers praised the local details after The Weeknd posted concert footage on Instagram, with some reflecting on the city’s familiar streets and sounds.

Director Evan Larsen told the South China Morning Post in an exclusive interview that the team made the video in about a week before its concert premiere. He pointed to nostalgia for the late 1980s and early 1990s as the key to its appeal. His account puts a clear period behind the images and the choice of Wong’s 1993 recording.

The local tribute arrived inside a much larger touring business. AllHipHop reported in November 2025 that the “After Hours Til Dawn Tour” had passed $1 billion in gross revenue, with more than 7.5 million tickets sold over 153 shows.

His current Asia leg grew from 11 stadium shows to 17. It is set to finish with two Kuala Lumpur dates on November 4 and 5.

item.title: Grandmaster Flash Joins Al Sharpton To Revisit Hip-Hop’s Origins
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Grandmaster Flash discusses early Hip-Hop DJ techniques with Ari Melber and Al Sharpton during an October 23 MS NOW broadcast.
item.content:encoded:
Grandmaster Flash is taking the story of Hip-Hop’s first DJs to national television alongside Rev. Al Sharpton and Ari Melber.

The legendary Bronx DJ joined MS NOW’sbroadcast to discuss rap, politics and the craft behind his turntable innovations. Melber brought Flash and Sharpton together for a special edition of his recurring Fallback segment.

The exchange focused on the Quik Mix Theory, the method Flash developed to keep short musical breaks going for dancers. Using two copies of a record, a DJ could alternate the same drum passage without forcing the crowd to stop.

That skill helped create longer instrumental sections for early MCs and changed what performers could do at Bronx parties. Flash has also argued that building Hip-Hop involved many contributors, not a single inventor.

During an October interview, he described his role without taking sole credit for the culture. “This is my contributions to the culture. It’s called the quick mix theory. So for me, I’m only one part of this.”

His book Birth of a Culture examines why particular DJ techniques worked, tracing the physics and mathematics he used with turntables. Flash learned electronics as a child, taking apart household equipment before developing his own approach to playing records at Bronx neighborhood parties.

The pioneer described his musical outlook in a September conversation about his experiences with different records. “This is not a black thing or a white thing, or a wrong thing or a right thing,” he explained.

Flash described the first time his father’s record player caught his attention. “My dad is a magician! He’s the best in the world. I’m like, Holy moly, how did he do that?”

That childhood fascination eventually became a way to make dancers hear more of the music they loved, rather than just the short breaks.

The latest broadcaster reel connects that personal history to a wider conversation about Hip-Hop’s reach and cultural importance in America today.

The book arrived September 22 through Amistad, with journalist Robert “Scoop” Jackson serving as Flash’s co-author.

item.title: Jermaine Dupri Demands Spotify Pay Artists For AI Remixes: “Cut Us In”
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: Jermaine Dupri urges musicians to unite over Spotify's AI remix plans and seek a say in fees and which records can be used.
item.content:encoded:
Jermaine Dupri wants artists to name their price before Spotify lets subscribers use AI to make new versions of their songs.

The producer urged musicians to join forces in an October 31 Instagram post about the streaming service’s planned remix tool.

His demand went beyond getting paid for streams: artists should help set the fee and choose which records the tool can use.

“Whoever is behind this, believes they can change the landscape of music and take all the value away from the actual artist and producers who did it and give it to someone else,” Dupri wrote.

He called on artists to work together on terms before ending his caption with a blunt demand for the company.

“Whoever is behind this, believes they can change the landscape of music and take all the value away from the actual artist and producers who did it and give it to someone else, ok, So let’s play ball!! Spotify is scheduled to make $21.85 billion THIS year,so artist we need to come together and create a fee for what we want, and what songs we allow this to happen to, THEY GOTTA CUT US IN, OR CUT THIS SHIT OUT,” he wrote.

Spotify has described a paid extra for Premium subscribers that would use generative AI to help fans rework songs or record covers.

The company announced music licensing deals with Universal Music Group in May, followed by an agreement with Believe in October.

Spotify’s stated terms for Believe and TuneCore artists include voluntary participation and royalty payments when fans stream the versions made through the tool.

Artists served by those companies would first agree to consider AI programs, then make a separate choice about joining Spotify’s offer.

Each fan remix would also direct listeners to the source track and artist, giving the original music a path to more plays.

Those plans address permission and payment, though the announcement does not spell out the royalty split or a fee that artists could set themselves.

Dupri’s concerns about tech companies’ role in music predate this post, including his 2024 criticism of AI music generator Udio.

At the time, he challenged the idea that music workers should accept new rules from people who came from outside their business.

Spotify Co-CEO Alex Norström described the company’s approach when it announced the Universal deal, stressing the role of creators in that plan.

“What we’re building is grounded in consent, credit, and compensation for the artists and songwriters that take part,” he said.

Spotify’s May agreement with Universal also covered music publishing rights, bringing songwriters into the planned covers-and-remixes service alongside recording artists.

item.title: Keefe D Moved To Maximum-Security Prison After Tupac Murder Sentence
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Keefe D was moved to Nevada's High Desert State Prison after receiving 40 years to life for his role in Tupac Shakur's murder.
item.content:encoded:
Keefe D has been moved to High Desert State Prison to serve his sentence for Tupac Shakur’s murder, taking the case from a Las Vegas jail to Nevada’s maximum-security prison system.

The 63-year-old, whose legal name is Duane Davis, is now housed at the prison near Indian Springs. FOX5 Las Vegas confirmed his location through Nevada Department of Corrections records.

According to 8 News Now’s reporting, a corrections spokesperson said the move happened October 22. That was nine days after Judge Carli Kierny imposed his punishment.

The sentence requires Davis to serve at least 40 years before he can be considered for parole. He received credit for 731 days already spent in custody, according to 8 News Now.

TMZ’s follow-up showed a new prison mug shot credited to the Nevada Department of Corrections.

High Desert became Nevada’s maximum-security institution in 2024, replacing Ely State Prison. The Department of Corrections moved nearly 2,000 prisoners between the two facilities during that change.

Officials cited stronger staffing, access to outside medical care and law enforcement, and a more secure perimeter among the reasons for the switch. High Desert has two secure fences plus a high-voltage electric fence. It also houses people with different custody classifications.

Davis’ transfer followed a trial built largely around his own accounts of the killing.

A jury convicted him of first-degree murder with use of a deadly weapon on August 31. As AllHipHop previously reported, prosecutors argued Davis supplied the gun and helped organize retaliation after Tupac and his associates beat Davis’ nephew, Orlando Anderson, at the MGM Grand.

The prosecution’s case centered on Davis’ role in arranging the attack rather than firing the shots. Tupac was riding with Suge Knight when a gunman opened fire on September 7, 1996. The rapper died September 13 at 25.

Jurors heard Davis’ recorded police interview and material from his television appearances and memoir. His defense argued those stories were unreliable accounts meant to earn money. Davis did not testify at trial.

His legal team has maintained his innocence and said it plans to appeal the conviction.

item.title: RFK Jr. Leaves Anti-Arab Remarks Unanswered At Detroit Health Visit
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Robert F. Kennedy Jr. declined to address his false claims about Arab science as CAIR called for his removal from office.
item.content:encoded:
Robert F. Kennedy Jr. left his anti-Arab remarks unanswered at a Detroit health visit as a civil rights group demanded that he lose his Cabinet job.

The Council on American-Islamic Relations called for the health secretary’s immediate firing. The Muslim civil rights group tied its demand to his job running a federal agency whose work reaches Americans across ethnic and religious lines.

In its statement, CAIR called the remarks “utterly disqualifying for public office.” It also noted that his attack swept in Muslim and Christian Arab Americans.

Kennedy made the claims in Grand Rapids on October 26 while campaigning for Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers. Rogers is running against Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, who is Muslim and has an Arab family background.

“There are five hundred million Arabs in the world. And yet they don’t produce science,” Kennedy said, according to Michigan Advance. “They don’t win the Nobel Prize.”

The record includes winners from both science and literature. CAIR cited Egyptian-American chemist Ahmed Zewail, who won in 1999, and Egyptian novelist Naguib Mahfouz, who received the literature prize in 1988.

Omar Yaghi shared the 2025 chemistry prize with Richard Robson and Susumu Kitagawa. The UC Berkeley professor was born in Jordan to Palestinian refugees, according to his university.

Their work produced materials called metal-organic frameworks. Those structures have uses that include collecting water from dry air and trapping carbon dioxide. Yaghi’s award came the year before Kennedy’s claim.

Kennedy blamed the Muslim Brotherhood for the decline he alleged. El-Sayed has denied involvement with the group and publicly rejected it, Michigan Advance reported.

His public statements on science had drawn scrutiny before. AllHipHop previously covered Hillary Clinton’s criticism of Kennedy and President Donald Trump over their claims about vaccines and pregnancy medications in September 2025.

In Detroit, Kennedy instead discussed recovery services after visiting the Detroit Wayne Integrated Health Network. Michigan Advance reported that he did not address the anti-Arab comments while taking questions.

The visit concerned STREETS, a federal program for people facing homelessness and serious mental illness or substance use disorders. HHS announced that Detroit’s Health Department was among eight recipients sharing $96 million. Each was set to receive $3 million annually for four years to connect treatment with housing and other recovery support.

item.title: Be’n Original Enters Crime Fiction With Debut Novel Power Kingdom
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: Be'n Original swaps news deadlines for underworld fiction, introducing a debut thriller "Power Kingdom."
item.content:encoded:
Be’n Original, a former writer for AllHipHop, has evolved from covering culture to exploring criminal power in Power Kingdom, introducing his debut in fictional writing.

The veteran journalist and Urban Magazine publisher announced the urban crime thriller bringing his vast experience in entertainment media to a story about an expanding criminal empire.

For a writer whose bylines have appeared in AllHipHop, XXL, The Source, Vibe, King and Yahoo!, the move puts a different kind of storytelling at the center of his work. Instead of reporting on public figures and cultural developments, Be’n Original is introducing fictional characters whose personal relationships could threaten their survival.

Power Kingdom unfolds within a kingdom built on fear. According to the announcement, its premise draws inspiration from a popular colloquialism for Poughkeepsie, New York. The release does not identify that expression or provide further details about how the city informs the narrative.

The saga follows a growing criminal operation and a brotherhood operating in secrecy. The dangerous territory between them becomes a serious testing ground for loyalty as concealed motives emerge and relationships become liabilities.

The novel asks its characters to weigh love, honor, revenge and survival against one another. Closeness carries consequences in this world, where knowing someone’s secrets can create an advantage or expose a weakness. Friendship offers no guarantee of protection.

That focus gives the thriller a conflict beyond the expansion of a criminal enterprise. The announcement positions personal vulnerability as a central threat to authority, with those who command through intimidation facing the possibility that their control can collapse.

Be’n Original’s professional background includes journalism, publishing and creative direction.

The release is only the beginning and more on central characters are expected to be revealed.

The release date has not been announced yet.

Pre-orders for Power Kingdom by Be’n Original are now available: https://www.paypal.com/ncp/payment/X9RYANWSWVQSQ
